title: Can Large Language Models Capture Public Opinion about Global Warming? An Empirical Assessment of Algorithmic Fidelity and Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model prediction accuracy and F1 scores of voting behaviors and global warming beliefs against actual survey data across different racial and ethnic groups, specifically noting underestimations of Black Americans' views.

Evaluating the simulated survey responses of LLMs conditioned on political ideology and party affiliation against real human data to identify disparities, such as the models' overestimation of partisan polarization.
Assessing the algorithmic fidelity of simulated survey responses by comparing model predictions (accuracy and F1 scores) to actual human survey baselines segmented by gender.
Comparing the model's prediction accuracy and response distributions for climate beliefs and voting patterns across different age brackets using human survey data as the ground truth.
Measuring differences in model prediction performance and algorithmic fidelity when the LLMs are conditioned on various levels of educational attainment.
